note: Does the species floor (plan 012, ?procobjFloor) cost frame time? Claude, headless on the mac (DPR=2, capped/vsync), against build/original/opensa (the unbaked 2026-08-10 pak). Four single-scene country-dusk legs: TWO floor=0 arms and TWO floor=1 arms, so each side carries its own A/A drift (lesson 61 — the pair is what makes the verdict readable). Run order a0, a1, b0, b1. VERDICT: no resolvable cost. Triangles move +0.002 % (1191171 -> 1191191 as pair means) against a floor=0 pair spread of 0.011 %, and avgDrawCalls is 821 in every arm — which is what budget conservation predicts, since the floor pays for every rescued placement with the highest-lottery survivor rather than adding one. gpuMs.pass 3.6665 -> 3.6855 (+0.52 %) is the only column that moves at all, and the floor=0 pair's own drift is 0.30 % and the floor=1 pair's 0.14 %, so it is at the noise floor, not above it. READ THE SATURATION FIRST: this is the capped lane, so avgMs sits on 8.33 and p95Ms on 9.0-9.2 in all four arms and neither can answer a cost question (lessons 44/60); gpuMs.pass and avgTriangles are the readable columns. hitch.maxMs spans 9.5-31.8 with no relation to the arm (one slow frame in b0, none in b1) — the same no-relation-to-load pattern the 2026-08-10 ladder recorded. HONEST GAP: no positive control was run in THIS lane, so it is not established that the floor changes anything in country-dusk specifically; the visual A/B that proves the knob works was taken elsewhere (cell -5,7, the desert, with a 9.81 % control) and is recorded in plan 012, not here. What this run supports is 'no cost', not 'an effect was present and still cost nothing'.
